title: Study Abroad Experience at National Taiwan University
paragraphs: I used the opportunity of this study abroad program to study in Taiwan. Taiwan is a neighboring country of Japan less than three hours from Nagoya, an island country with a population of about 24 million, and one of Japan's friendly countries, with nearly 4 million people a year visiting Japan. I myself had traveled to Taiwan several times and felt close to it, and I also wanted to become able to speak Chinese well, so I very much wanted to study in Taiwan.

I entered Taiwan on February 28 and moved into the Jingfu Hall dormitory of National Taiwan University. I arrived two weeks before the start of the clerkship because I wanted to attend a local language school and get used to Chinese conversation. There I took private lessons at a language school called TLI. From March 14, I did four weeks of Emergency Medicine, four weeks of Family Medicine, and two weeks each of obstetrics and gynecology and pediatrics. Taking histories from local patients in Chinese, however clumsily, and discussing diseases with the doctors was a very good experience. In addition, I used my days off to travel around Taiwan and to Hong Kong and Xiamen and experience the local culture. The experience of speaking to local people in Chinese while they were speaking their local language and being able to converse in Chinese made me feel the strength of Chinese, which has a large speaking population, and I felt firsthand how narrow a world I had been in.

That I was able to gain so many experiences that will nourish my life in this valuable study abroad is thanks to Dr. 長谷川 and Dr. 粕屋, the doctors of the Frontier Society who cheered me on, Mr. I-Wen Chang of National Taiwan University, Dr. Rui-Sheng Yan, Dr. Shin-Yu, Dr. Chin-Der Chen and Dr. Shao-Yi Cheng, and my roommates at Jingfu Hall and the local students and exchange students. Thank you very much. I would like to take this opportunity to express my thanks.
